is_anopheles.evidence: Page 4 notes that malaria transmission in all trial sites was from mosquitoes belonging to the Anopheles gambiae s.l. species complex and Anopheles funestus.

reports_target_markers.evidence: Page 19 and Page 51 report kdr 1014F (Vgsc L995F), 1014S (Vgsc L995S), and Ace-1 G119S (Ace-1 G280S) alleles from included primary studies.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Page 51 (Analysis 1.5) presents kdr allele counts from Corbel 2012 (e.g. 52/61 and 39/46).

african_field_population.evidence: Page 4 reports trials conducted on field mosquito populations in Benin, Tanzania, Sudan, The Gambia, and Eritrea.

is_primary_study.evidence: Page 1 states this is a Cochrane Systematic Review ('Indoor residual spraying for preventing malaria in communities using insecticide-treated nets (Review)').

sub_country_location.evidence: Page 28 (Ouidah-Kpomasse-Tori Bossito health district, Benin), Page 31 (Galabat, Sudan), Page 38 (Muleba District, Tanzania).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Primary studies included in the review report specific collection windows <=3 years (e.g., Corbel 2012 from 2008-2009, Kafy 2017 from 2012-2015).

duplicate_risk.evidence: This Cochrane review re-analyses and synthesizes data from previously published primary trials (Corbel 2012, Kafy 2017, Keating 2011, Pinder 2015, Protopopoff 2018, West 2014).

supplement.evidence: Not applicable because the study is ineligible as a systematic review.

assessment.summary: This Cochrane systematic review summarizes evidence from six cluster-randomized trials across sub-Saharan Africa assessing the additional benefit of indoor residual spraying (IRS) when combined with insecticide-treated nets (ITNs). Because it is a systematic review re-analysing published data rather than a primary empirical study, it is ineligible.
exclusion_reasons: The study is a systematic review / meta-analysis and not a primary empirical study.
